user.title: Connect to your inverter
user.description:
Home Assistant talks to the inverter directly over Modbus, on your own network — the SEMS cloud account is not involved.

Most people use **Modbus TCP**: the inverter or its Wi-Fi/LAN dongle has an IP address, and that is all you need. Pick a serial option only if you wired an RS485 adapter to the inverter's COM port.

Fill in only the fields that match the connection you chose; the others are ignored.

data_description.connection: Modbus TCP for a normal Wi-Fi or LAN dongle. RTU over TCP if a serial-to-Ethernet gateway (Elfin, USR, Waveshare) sits in between. Serial if the adapter is plugged into the machine running Home Assistant.
data_description.host: TCP only. Look it up in your router's device list, or in the SolarGo app under network settings. Reserve a fixed address for it in the router, otherwise the connection breaks the next time the lease changes. Example: 192.168.1.50
data_description.port: 502 for a GoodWe dongle. Change it only if your gateway uses something else — 8899 is a common alternative.
data_description.serial_port: Serial only. Usually /dev/ttyUSB0 on Home Assistant OS. Check Settings › System › Hardware if unsure.
data_description.baudrate: Serial only. GoodWe uses 9600 unless you changed it on the inverter.
data_description.slave: 247 on virtually every GoodWe inverter. Try 1 only if 247 does not answer.

battery.title: Battery, prices and dispatch
battery.description:
These settings tell the integration how much energy it may move and when moving it is worth the wear. The defaults fit a typical 10 kWh home battery, so if a field means nothing to you, leave it alone — everything here can be changed later from the integration's **Configure** button.

Live values (state of charge, power) are read from the inverter itself; nothing below has to match a sensor.

data.enable_dispatch: Let this integration control the inverter
data.hold_for_peak: Save the battery for the evening peak
data.scan_interval: How often to read the inverter

data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: Off the battery label or datasheet — 10 for a 10 kWh pack. Only used when the battery's BMS does not report its own capacity.
data_description.min_soc: The reserve you keep for the house. Charge is never sold or self-consumed below this level; 15% is a sane balance between usable energy and battery life.
data_description.target_soc: Where charging in cheap hours stops. Must be higher than the reserve above. 95% avoids the slow, inefficient last few percent.
data_description.max_charge_power_w: Do not exceed your inverter's battery rating — about 4600 W on a 10 kW hybrid. Set it lower to charge more gently.
data_description.max_discharge_power_w: Normally the same as the charge power.
data_description.enable_dispatch: Leave this off for a read-only start: you get every sensor and the day-ahead prices, and nothing is ever written to the inverter. When you do turn it on, the integration switches between charging, discharging and self-consumption by itself. There is also a 'Price dispatch' switch to flip it any time.
data_description.hold_for_peak: The battery stops discharging during the cheap afternoon so the energy is still there for the expensive evening hours. Useful when your evening consumption is high; leave it off if you would rather always cover the current load.
data_description.cycle_cost_lei_mwh: Battery wear, expressed per MWh cycled. It stops the integration from cycling the battery for a price difference too small to be worth it. Rough estimate: battery price ÷ (warranted cycles × capacity in MWh). 150 RON/MWh is a reasonable starting point; raise it to trade less.
data_description.round_trip_efficiency: How much of the stored energy you get back out. 0.90 means 90%, typical for a lithium battery behind a hybrid inverter.
data_description.entsoe_token: Day-ahead prices come from OPCOM PZU and need no account. A free ENTSO-E token (request one by email from transparency.entsoe.eu) is used as a fallback when OPCOM cannot be reached.
data_description.soc_entity: Leave this empty. It is only needed if your BMS does not report state of charge over Modbus, in which case pick any sensor that shows the battery percentage.
data_description.scan_interval: 30 seconds suits almost everyone. Much faster and some inverters start ignoring Modbus requests.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the inverter. Check the IP address and port, make sure the inverter is on the same network, and close any other app holding the Modbus connection (SEMS/SolarGo or a second Modbus integration).
error.serial_port_required: Enter the serial device, for example /dev/ttyUSB0.
error.target_below_min: 'Charge up to' has to be higher than 'Never discharge below'.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant log for details.

init.title: Battery, prices and dispatch
init.description: Anything here can be changed at any time; the integration reloads with the new values. Connection settings are not shown — remove and re-add the integration to change those.
